title: Before your first visit
summary: What to bring and what happens at a first appointment.
body:
Bring a list of any medicines you take and your insurance card if you have one. If you have old x-rays from another dentist, we can ask for them with your permission.

A first visit takes about seventy-five minutes: x-rays, a cleaning, an exam with the dentist and time to talk.

If you are nervous, say so when you book. We will give you a longer appointment and stop whenever you raise a hand.

title: If you are nervous about the dentist
summary: How we slow things down for anxious patients, including sedation for longer treatments.
body:
About one in five of our patients tells us they are nervous. We agree a stop signal before we start, explain each step before we do it, and never rush.

For wisdom teeth and implants, we can offer oral sedation. You will need someone to drive you home.

title: A first visit for children
summary: Bringing a child for the first time, from around their first birthday.
body: The first visit is short: a ride in the chair, a count of the teeth and a look at how they are coming in. We see children from their first birthday.

title: After a filling
timeline: 0~Numb for two to three hours. Do not chew on that side until it wears off|24~Mild sensitivity to cold is normal|168~If the bite feels high after a week, call us for a two-minute adjustment
summary: What to expect in the hours and days after a filling.
body:
The filling is fully hard when you leave. Avoid chewing on the numb side so you do not bite your cheek.

Sensitivity to cold can last a week or two after a deep filling. If it gets worse rather than better, call us.

title: Caring for a temporary crown
timeline: 0~Numb for two to three hours|24~Gum around the tooth may be tender|72~Tenderness settles|336~Final crown fitted at about two weeks
summary: Keeping a temporary crown in place until the final one is ready.
body:
Avoid sticky and very hard food on that side. Floss by sliding the floss out sideways rather than pulling it up.

If the temporary comes off, keep it and call us. You can put it back with a little toothpaste until we see you.

title: After a root canal
timeline: 0~Numb for two to three hours|24~The tooth may ache when you bite|72~Aching settles for most people|504~Book the crown within three weeks
summary: What to expect after a root canal and why the crown matters.
body:
A dull ache when you bite is normal for a few days. Over-the-counter pain relief usually handles it.

Until the crown is fitted, the tooth has a temporary filling and is more likely to crack, so chew on the other side.

title: After a deep cleaning
timeline: 0~Numb for two to three hours|24~Gums tender, some bleeding when brushing|72~Tenderness settles|1008~Gums measured again at six weeks
summary: Looking after your gums after a deep cleaning.
body: Rinse with warm salt water twice a day for three days. Keep brushing and flossing, gently: the gums heal faster when they are clean.

title: After wisdom tooth removal
timeline: 0~Bite on the gauze for 30 to 45 minutes|2~Take the first dose of pain relief before the numbness wears off|24~No rinsing, spitting or straws for the first day|72~Swelling peaks on day two or three, then settles|168~Short check visit at one week|336~Most people feel normal by two weeks
summary: What to do, hour by hour, after wisdom teeth come out.
body:
Rest with your head raised on the first evening. Cold packs on the cheek help for the first day; warm compresses help after that.

Soft food for three days. From the second day, rinse gently with warm salt water after meals.

Call us if the pain gets worse after day three, or if you have a fever.

title: After an implant
timeline: 0~Bite on gauze for 30 minutes|24~Some swelling and bruising is normal|72~Most people are back to work|336~Stitches dissolve|2160~Healing check at three months
summary: Looking after the implant site while it heals.
body:
Do not chew on the implant side until we say so. Brush the area gently from the second day.

Smoking slows healing and is the most common reason implants fail. If you smoke, we will talk about it before the surgery.

title: After an extraction
timeline: 0~Bite on the gauze for 30 minutes|24~No rinsing, spitting or straws|72~Soreness settles|168~Socket closing over
summary: What to do after a tooth is removed.
body: Keep the blood clot in place for the first day: no rinsing, spitting, straws or smoking. Soft food on the other side.

title: Whitening at home
timeline: 0~Wear the trays for thirty minutes a day|72~Sensitivity, if you get it, peaks around day three|336~Done after two weeks
summary: How to use your trays and gel.
body:
A small drop of gel in each tooth of the tray is enough. Wipe off any gel that gets onto your gums.

If your teeth feel sensitive, skip a day.

title: A day with clear aligners
timeline: 0~Wear them 22 hours a day|48~Each new aligner feels tight for about two days|1344~Check visit every eight weeks
summary: Wearing, cleaning and swapping your aligners.
body: Take the aligners out to eat or drink anything but water. Brush before you put them back in.

title: Looking after your night guard
summary: Cleaning and storing a night guard.
body: Brush it with cold water and a soft brush each morning, and keep it in its case. Hot water warps it.

title: Brushing and flossing at home
summary: Two minutes, twice a day, and the part most people miss.
body:
Angle the brush toward the gumline. Floss before you brush so the fluoride reaches between the teeth.

The inside of the lower front teeth is where most people miss.

title: When something goes wrong
summary: What to do if a tooth breaks, a crown comes off or your face swells.
body: If a tooth breaks, keep the piece and call us. If your face swells and it is hard to swallow or breathe, go to the emergency room.

title: Medical history form
summary: The health questions we ask every patient, printable to fill in at home.
body:
Section 1. Medicines you take, with the dose.

Section 2. Allergies, including latex and any reaction to local anesthetic.

Section 3. Heart conditions, joint replacements, diabetes, pregnancy.

This is a fictional sample form. Bring the printed copy to your visit; there is nothing to submit online.

title: Consent for a child's treatment
summary: For a parent or guardian to sign before a child's treatment.
body:
Name of the child, the treatment, and the signature of a parent or guardian.

Fictional sample form for a printed copy.

title: Records release form
summary: To ask your previous dentist to send us your x-rays and records.
body:
Your previous dentist's name and address, the records you want sent, and your signature.

Fictional sample form for a printed copy.
